title: 50,000 game ready, open-source assets and game systems [Link Included]
author: Important-Respect-12
selftext:
Hey everyone, I did a post here yesterday that was removed because our asset library was gated by download and sign in. We have now published the open-source toolbox online and it's not gated by download or sign in to access. 

This library includes 50,000 3D models, textures, 2D assets, splats, sounds, and music. More than 5000 of the assets are made by us, and the rest is from different open source asset stores, that we put in one place that is searchable through a CLI and MCP (free) so that your agents access everything in the toolbox easily.

We also made a major addition: We are open-sourcing systems like procedural dungeons, physics engines, crowd navigation, car driving mechanics, procedural terrain generation, tree generators etc. 

We made this because we want to construct bigger blocks that developers can use in their games. These blocks can then be edited in any way to look completely different than the system itself 

Link: [https://patch.gg/create/toolbox/assets](https://patch.gg/create/toolbox/assets) 

Note: Viewing the library requires no sign-in or download. Downloading requires sign in to prevent bot attacks (as most open-source assets stores), but it is completely free to download and open-source so you can add anything you like in your game! 

Hope you find this useful, as I said, we're planning to open-source 10,000 more assets so please tell us what you'd like us to add! (systems included)

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
lol you have no idea what you’re talking about then.

“Better polycounts” means what? The creator chooses the polygon budget. Tripo, Meshy and Rodin all let you set face targets and choose triangle or quad output.  
You can prefer Tripo’s results, sure.

But knowing the generator still doesn’t tell you which settings were used, whether the meshes were retopologized afterward, or what’s actually in this pack. If poly count and topology are your concern, ask for the counts and wireframes so “Made with Tripo” doesn’t answer either.

**You don’t even know when they were made. Were they made when Tripo was better or Meshy or neither?  Cmon.**

replies.author: Aineisa
replies.body:
1k tris in meshy won’t have the same quality as 1k in tripo in my opinion. 

The model does matter.

replies.author: romansamurai
replies.body:
Nah. I’ve been using both for the last four to six months. In my experience, they keep leapfrogging each other, so you’re explaining this with way more confidence than you should lol.

Last month, Tripo was blowing my mind with quality. Recently, its results have gotten noticeably worse for me, while Meshy 7 has been excellent, especially for characters generated from a single reference image. 

Right now, Meshy is comfortably beating what I’m getting from Tripo there. Text to 3D, I might still give Tripo the edge…for this model.

If you want you can look at the benchmarks Meshy  7 and 7.1 is ranked above Tripo 3.1 overall. But last month Top3D’s geometry rankings put Tripo 3.1 above both. 

Even Meshy’s own geometry benchmark changes winners depending on the input: Meshy 7 wins all three single view metrics, while Tripo wins two of three with four views.

Yes, the model matters. So do the version, input, settings and what you’re judging. So if they made assets with one or the other when they were at peak…how will you know?  

Last month I would’ve picked Tripo for work I’m choosing Meshy for today. Another update could change that again. 

So your “Tripo has better polycounts and topology” isn’t going to fly. Especially in this situation.
